content:
Lauren Bishop: Getting a bunch of the same q’s from ABM calls: how are we cleanly positioning Dedicated vs Private for regulated buyers without sounding like “Private is the only compliant option”? Also folks keep asking for a pricing/packaging one-liner (what’s the commercial construct + when does compliance addendum kick in). Can we align and update the pricing guidance page?

Soojin Lee: +1. In 2 calls this week the buyer heard “Dedicated” and assumed it meant “single-tenant + VPC.” We need a crisp decision tree and consistent language for outbound + discovery.

Stephanie Nguyen: From the field: CISOs keep asking “Do we need Private to pass our security review?” Platform teams ask “Is Dedicated enough to get predictable throughput + isolate from other customers?” We need to answer both quickly.

Vivek Kulkarni: Proposed positioning (sanity check):
- Dedicated = reserved GPU capacity + predictable throughput/latency, data isolation at the compute pool level, Redwood-operated environment. Best when: you want performance SLOs + isolation, but you don’t require private networking / customer-controlled perimeter.
- Private = customer-controlled network boundary (VPC / on-prem), tighter integration w/ customer IAM + key management options, and deployment flexibility for residency / restricted egress. Best when: VPC-only requirement, strict data boundary, on-prem/air-gapped, or internal policy demands customer-managed networking.

Vivek Kulkarni: Important nuance: regulated != automatically Private. Some regulated workloads can run on Dedicated if policies allow managed service + we meet controls (audit logs, SSO/SAML, retention policy, etc.).

Naomi Feldman: +1 on nuance. Please don’t let this turn into “Dedicated is not compliant.” We should phrase it as “deployment model choice is driven by your control requirements.” Also: avoid “HIPAA-ready” / “guaranteed compliance.” Use “supports common controls required in regulated environments” + point to Security FAQ/evidence pack process.

Markus Klein: From SE side, I’d love a simple set of discovery questions:
1) Do you require VPC-only connectivity or private link (no public internet)?
2) Any on-prem/air-gapped requirement?
3) Key management: customer-managed KMS/HSM required?
4) Data residency + retention: do you need customer-configurable retention windows + export?
If yes to 1/2 (or hard yes to 3 depending on policy) => lean Private.
If no and main driver is predictable performance + isolation => Dedicated.

Lauren Bishop: That matches how I’ve been doing it, but we need PMM-approved copy for AEs/SDRs.

Soojin Lee: Suggested “talk track” language (draft):
- “Dedicated gives you predictable capacity and isolation with Redwood managing the environment. It’s the fastest path to performance SLOs when your security team is comfortable with a managed deployment.”
- “Private is for orgs that need the inference stack inside their network boundary (VPC or on-prem), with stricter controls around connectivity and infrastructure ownership.”
We should add: “Both support audit logs, RBAC/SSO options, and defined retention policies; the difference is where the deployment lives and who controls the perimeter.”

Stephanie Nguyen: Also add a line on procurement: for some accounts, “Private” automatically maps to enterprise + longer security/procurement cycle. AEs need to set expectations.

Sofia Mendes: Commercial construct bullets we should standardize (internal guidance only):
- Dedicated: monthly/annual capacity commit (GPU pool) + support tier; optional compliance add-ons depending on retention/logging needs.
- Private: platform fee + support tier + (if applicable) deployment/implementation services; can be transacted via direct order form or AWS Marketplace private offer.
We should be careful about quoting list prices in Slack—just define structure + when to pull in Legal/Finance.

Naomi Feldman: +1, and add the “when to involve Security” trigger: any custom audit/retention language, residency commitments, or non-standard questionnaire timelines.

Kira Thompson: I can update the internal pricing guidance page, but I need:
1) Final decision tree wording (PMM + Product)
2) “Do/Don’t say” callouts (Security)
3) A short section on “common misconceptions” (Dedicated != VPC; Private != automatically required)

Elliot Price: Loop me in on the doc update. We should link it from the regulated landing page / enablement deck (internal only) and keep it consistent with the compliance addendum notes. Also: add a quick “starter email snippet” for AEs.

Lauren Bishop: Action: Kira + Elliot can you update the pricing guidance page this week? We need it before the next outbound wave.

Soojin Lee: I’ll post final PMM copy by EOD tomorrow. Naomi, can you review for claims sensitivity?

Naomi Feldman: Yes. Please include the exact line about evidence pack sharing (NDA / controlled distribution) so we don’t ad-lib.

Markus Klein: I’ll add the discovery question block + a 1-slide decision tree we can paste into the enablement deck.

Sofia Mendes: Also note: if customer asks for DPA/SLA redlines specific to data residency/retention, AEs should route to Legal early (don’t promise “we can do X” in-email).

Kira Thompson: Got it. I’ll draft the update and share in #docs for review. Target: PR by Thursday. Please tag me if there’s a single source of truth doc I should align with.

Elliot Price: Use the existing internal page: “Private deployments compliance addendum pricing notes” as base; we’ll append the Dedicated vs Private positioning section and add a TL;DR.

Lauren Bishop: Perfect. Thanks all. Let’s keep the language consistent across SDR sequences + deck + landing page footnotes.
